confirmed: The single sac, RECEIVE x2, Pac SEND, DOCK, and two-tier exits form the main resource-transfer plan proposed in pass one.

missed_mechanics: Pac plus the sac supply exactly two weights on RECEIVE; Isp RELEASE latches the first stage.
Pac SEND is a hold-powered vertical return lift that must be parked by stepping off; DOCK is a hold that keeps the final wall open.
RELEASE also starts Cana's temporary boomerang interference.
incorrect_inferences: The first pass left RECEIVE x2 and power links unknown rather than asserting a false mechanic; its implied hazard concern from upper falls is resolved by the continuous safe floor.
changed_judgments: Execution 2 to 3 because the actual route needs several cargo/lift transfers and controlled ledge movements.
Timing null to 2 because parking the powered return lift involves a repeatable height window.
Hazards null to 0 because falls reach a full-width safe floor and temporary SHOVE/DIZZY do not create mandatory lethal exposure here.
Novelty 3 to 2 because Cargo Exchange already taught cargo-plus-hero weight and two-tier handoff; this is one new recombination.
Recovery null to 2 because mistaken SEND timing or a knockoff requires reactivation and some repositioning without a full reset.

unresolved: No novice data show whether pairs infer the complete sac itinerary from labels or recover smoothly from SEND interference.

single_operator_note: A single operator must coordinate Isp's upper cargo handling with Pac's lower RECEIVE and SEND holds; this is extra sequential control burden outside the two-human scores.
